answer: To limit sybil accounts, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it can earn reputation or receive work. A challenge protocol randomly selects identities for costly audits; proven duplicate control forfeits their stake, while passing leaves it locked until the audit window closes. This does not make identities impossible to fake, but makes many identities expensive: an attacker must fund each bond and risk losing it. An atlas of accounts, a marble-sized stake, or nectar rewards cannot bypass that liability.
